correctness.rationale: PASS: Simple spectrum follows from the nonvanishing Jacobi recurrence. The eigenprojector Hadamard sum gives B B^T with B consisting of squared normalized eigenvector components. Backward polynomials have parity and nonzero leading coefficients, yielding a Vandermonde in squared eigenvalues, hence rank equals count of distinct eigenvalue squares. Product of eigenvector norms comes from continuant resultants; cancellation yields det Mhat=prod_{i<j}(lambda_i+lambda_j)^2/Disc(chi). With chi_tau=P-tau Q and opposite parities, opposite-root resultant and chi_tau(0) produce L tau^{2floor(n/2)}/D0. At tau=0 the path is bipartite and squared eigenvalues have ceil(n/2) distinct values; at tau!=0 opposite pairs cannot occur. Independent SymPy exact-rational diagonal-moment Gram calculations reproduced determinant and rank for six separate small weighted signed/zero-potential cases; the all-n conclusion is analytic.

value.rationale: PASS: The average-mixing rank is a natural structural invariant of continuous quantum walks. This exact all-order weighted-path formula proves that any arbitrarily small endpoint defect removes the bipartite squared-eigenvalue degeneracy, quantitatively determining the vanishing determinant exponent and prefactor. That sharp classification is useful for perturbation/spectral mixing analysis independent of transfer-fidelity claims.

final_claim: For any n>=2, positive weighted path couplings a_j and one first-endpoint diagonal potential tau, Cesaro quantum average mixing has determinant (prod a_j^{2(n-j)}/D0) tau^{2 floor(n/2)} / Disc(chi_tau) and rank n iff tau!=0, else ceil(n/2); D0 is product of squared odd-index couplings for even n and squared even-index couplings for odd n.
limitations: Only endpoint potential; nonzero couplings; interior diagonal zero; Cesaro time averaging.
Determinant tends to zero as tau tends to zero, so no uniform spectral gap is claimed.
